title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## RoboHarm safety benchmark

### The Breakthrough
A new benchmark called RoboHarm evaluates robot policies on five deliberately harmful instructions using bimanual I2RT YAM arms, running 300 trials (20 per policy per instruction). It quantifies safety refusals versus completions and finds that more capable models refuse fewer unsafe requests, with statistically significant differences (p < 0.001).

### The Caveats
The benchmark measures only three policies and offers no established baseline or prior safety system for comparison, leaving improvement unclear.

## Workspace Models token memory

### The Breakthrough
Vision‑language supervision creates a compact workspace token that replaces raw observations at inference, removing costly VLM queries and improving success rates on memory‑intensive manipulation tasks in both simulation and real‑robot experiments.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no quantitative comparison to existing memory‑compression or VLM‑in‑loop baselines, so the improvement is unverified.

## StageGuard hierarchical transitions

### The Breakthrough
StageGuard uses agentic distillation where a teacher VLM explains subtask completion and a lightweight student VLM, fine‑tuned on these explanations, predicts stage transitions online with higher accuracy and low latency for real‑time robot monitoring.

### The Caveats
The claimed improvement lacks comparison to existing real‑time transition baselines.

## FAMOS articulation modeling

### The Breakthrough
The Multi‑state Articulation Transformer fuses sparse partial point clouds via alternating state‑wise and global attention and an articulation span loss, achieving consistent gains on PartNet‑Mobility, ACD, and ArtiCraft‑10K over prior feed‑forward and optimization methods.

### The Caveats
The paper does not name or describe the baselines it claims to outperform, making the gains unverifiable.

## SafeHarness obstacle‑aware coding agents

### The Breakthrough
SafeHarness adds obstacle‑aware route planning and contact execution harnesses to coding agents, raising task success to 71.9% and collision avoidance to 87.5%, a 6.5%/27.0% gain over SOTA and 2.3×/1.5× over the same agent without harnesses.

### The Caveats
Results are shown only in simulation; no real‑world robot experiments confirm the approach.

## Copper deterministic robot runtime

### The Breakthrough
Copper compiles static task graphs into a zero‑allocation Rust runtime that records deterministic ".copper" logs, supports ROS 2 via Zenoh, and runs on Linux, macOS, SBCs, and STM32H7 microcontrollers.

### The Caveats
No quantitative performance data or baseline comparisons are provided, leaving its advantages unclear.

## GPT‑6 Astra speculative capabilities

### The Breakthrough
According to a Hacker News post, Astra can generate and edit Blender scenes by looping code‑write‑render‑inspect, produce direct robot control signals, and orchestrate tool‑calling pipelines for embodied tasks using massive compute and RL fine‑tuning.

### The Caveats
Only speculative demos are offered; there are no real‑world robot experiments or quantitative benchmarks to verify the claims.

## Franken Surveillance System design

### The Breakthrough
The system defines four operational planes and an immutable EvidenceDeltaBatch stream, implements semantic MVCC and certified graph intelligence in pure Rust, and includes a digital‑twin workflow to link camera views into a metric 3D reconstruction.

### The Caveats
Only design documents and contract skeletons are provided, with no functional sensor integration or end‑to‑end evaluation.

## SAGE persistent identity kernel

### The Breakthrough
SAGE implements a consciousness‑loop architecture with metabolic states, multi‑path memory, and a plugin framework for tools and effectors, running 21 instances across eight machines and logging over 2,700 developmental sessions.

### The Caveats
The repository reports internal fleet statistics without benchmark datasets or performance metrics, so the claimed benefits are unvalidated.

### Priority
The RoboHarm benchmark is the most critical story because it delivers concrete real‑world safety data for robot policies, highlighting urgent risks and measurable gaps.

### One action
Review the RoboHarm methodology and consider adding similar harmful‑instruction safety tests to your own policy evaluation pipeline.
